children: CoreWeave signed Q3 short-dated contracts (≈3–6 months) priced at ≈$40M per MW and, as of Aug 11, 2026, increased total contracted power to ≈4.2 GW from ≈3.7 GW on Jun 30. It previously added over $25B of net new customer commitments early Q3.
Implies stronger unit economics; supports near-term revenue per capacity.
Short durations allow quicker repricing but add renewal risk.
Signals capacity scale-up; supports revenue runway if deliveries align.
Sequential growth indicates accelerating demand for compute.
Large demand sign; not yet in Jun 30 backlog, aiding future visibility.

This update reinforces a mid-cycle trend of rising AI compute demand and CoreWeave’s ability to reprice capacity higher. A larger catalyst would be converting commitments to backlog/revenue and demonstrating sustained $/MW pricing as more power and clusters come online.
Based on the original press release from CoreWeave, Inc. distributed by BusinessWire.
